## Definitions

- [fact] Stage meanings per MongoDB: COLLSCAN is a collection scan, IXSCAN an index scan, FETCH reads full documents, PROJECTION filters returned fields in memory, and SORT means documents were sorted in memory (or a covered index was used). A filter or sort that shows COLLSCAN would benefit from an index; docsExamined appears on COLLSCAN and FETCH stages and keysExamined on IXSCAN. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/explain-slow-queries/ · keywords: database profiler, executionStats, explain plan, index, plan stage, Explain Plan Interpretation
- [passage] Where `<string>>` is the field that is indexed and `<value>` is either the direction of the index, or the special index type such as `text` or `2dsphere`. See [index types](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types.md#std-label-index-types) for the full list of index types. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.stats.md#index-filter-behavior · keywords: index, index bounds, query settings, <string>>, <value>, text
- [passage] - If the `$facet` stage is the first stage in a pipeline, the stage will perform a `COLLSCAN`. The `$facet` stage does not make use of indexes if it is the first stage in the pipeline. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/facet.md#index-use · keywords: database profiler, index, plan stage, $facet, COLLSCAN
- [passage] For example, in the following document, `metadata` is a good choice of `metaField` since it makes it easy to query data from a given weather sensor. Using these fields, MongoDB buckets readings from a single sensor together. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md#how-the-metafield-affects-bucketing · keywords: executionStats, metadata, metaField
- [passage] The default name for an index is the concatenation of the indexed keys and each key's direction in the index (`1` or `-1`) using underscores as a separator. For example, an index created on `{ item : 1, quantity: -1 }` has the name `item_1_quantity_-1`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes.md#index-names · keywords: index, index bounds,  or , { item : 1, quantity: -1 }, item_1_quantity_-1

## Structure and components

- [passage] | Field | Description | Applicable Stages | | --- | --- | --- | | `docsExamined` | Specifies the number of documents scanned during the query execution stage. | `COLLSCAN`, `FETCH` | | `keysExamined` | For query execution stages that scan an index `keysExamined` is the total number of in-bounds and out-of-bounds keys that are examined in the process of the index scan. If the index scan consists of a single contiguous range of keys, only in-bounds keys need to be examined. If the index bounds consists of several key ranges, the index scan execution process may examine out-of-bounds keys in order to skip from the end of one range to the beginning of the next. | `IXSCAN` | | `numReads` | The number of documents scanned or index keys examined during the query execution stage. **New in version 5.1** | `COLLSCAN`, `IXSCAN` | | `seeks` | The number of times that we had to seek the index cursor to a new position in order to complete the index scan. | `IXSCAN` | | `usedDisk` | Whether the stage wrote to disk. **New in version 5.3** | `GROUP` | | `spills` | The number of times the stage spilled to disk. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledBytes` | The total amount of data written to disk in bytes. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledRecords` | The total number of individual records spilled to disk. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledDataStorageSize` | The total disk space, in bytes, used by the spilled data. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `peakTrackedMemBytes` | **New in version 8.3** Maximum number of bytes of tracked memory in use by the current query operation. Starting in MongoDB 9.0, the `COUNT_SCAN`, `GEO_NEAR_2D`, `GEO_NEAR_2DSPHERE`, and `UPDATE` stages also report this field. | `COUNT_SCAN`, `GEO_NEAR_2D`, `GEO_NEAR_2DSPHERE`, `GROUP`, `SORT`, `UPDATE` | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: database profiler, executionStats, explain plan, index, index bounds, plan stage
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 5.3, if the query planner selects a [clustered index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.createcollection.md#std-label-db.createCollection.clusteredIndex) for a [clustered collection](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections.md#std-label-clustered-collections) and the query contains bounds that define the portion of the index to search, the explain result includes a `CLUSTERED_IXSCAN` stage. The stage includes information about the clustered index key and index bounds. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#collection-scan · keywords: database profiler, index, index bounds, plan stage, query planner, CLUSTERED_IXSCAN · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] If the query planner selects a [clustered index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.createcollection.md#std-label-db.createCollection.clusteredIndex) for a [clustered collection](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections.md#std-label-clustered-collections) and the query *does not* contain bounds, the query performs an unbounded collection scan and the explain result includes a `COLLSCAN` stage. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#collection-scan · keywords: database profiler, index, index bounds, plan stage, query planner, COLLSCAN
- [passage] If the query planner selects a clustered index for a clustered collection and the query does not contain bounds, the query performs an unbounded collection scan and the explain result includes a COLLSCAN stage. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: database profiler, index, index bounds, plan stage, query planner
- [passage] Each stage consists of information specific to the stage. For example, an `IXSCAN` stage includes the index bounds along with other data specific to the index scan. If a stage has a child stage or multiple child stages, the stage will have an `inputStage` or `inputStages`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: explain plan, index, index bounds, plan stage, IXSCAN, inputStage · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/

- [passage] Contains *partial* execution information captured during the [plan selection phase](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-query-plans-query-optimization) for both the winning and rejected plans. The field is present only if `explain` runs in `allPlansExecution` verbosity mode. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, query planner, explain, allPlansExecution
- [passage] The `explain` results present the query plans as a tree of stages. The output structure can differ based on which query engine the operation uses. Operations can use the classic query engine or the [slot-based execution query engine.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/sbe.md#std-label-sbe-landing) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#explain-output-structure · keywords: explain plan, query planner, slot-based execution engine, explain
- [passage] If query settings are set, `querySettings` contains details about the query settings that are applied to the query shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: explain plan, query settings, query shape, querySettings · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] Contains information on the selection of the query plan by the [query optimizer.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-read-operations-query-optimization) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: explain plan, query optimization, query planner
- [passage] The explain results present the query plans as a tree of stages. The output structure can differ based on which query engine the operation uses. Operations can use the classic query engine or the slot-based execution query engine. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: explain plan, query planner, slot-based execution engine
- [passage] Contains statistics that describe the completed query execution for the winning plan. For write operations, completed query execution refers to the modifications that *would* be performed, but does *not* apply the modifications to the database. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: explain plan, query planner · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] Total time in milliseconds required for query plan selection and query execution. It includes the time it takes to run the trial phase part of the plan selection process, but does not include the network time to transmit the data back to the client. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: explain plan, query planner · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/

- [passage] [`explain.executionStats.totalDocsExamined`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.executionStats.totalDocsExamined) refers to the total number of documents examined and *not* to the number of documents returned. For example, a stage can examine a document in order to apply a filter. If the document is filtered out, then it has been examined but will not be returned as part of the query result set. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, explain.executionStats.totalDocsExamined · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/

The field is present only if `explain` runs in `executionStats` verbosity mode or higher and if `profileOperationResourceConsumptionMetrics` is enabled. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, explain, profileOperationResourceConsumptionMetrics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/

- [passage] For query execution stages that scan an index keysExamined is the total number of in-bounds and out-of-bounds keys that are examined in the process of the index scan. If the index scan consists of a single contiguous range of keys, only in-bounds keys need to be examined. If the index bounds consists of several key ranges, the index scan execution process may examine out-of-bounds keys in order to skip from the end of one range to the beginning of the next. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: executionStats, index, index bounds

- [passage] Specifies the number of "work units" performed by the query execution stage. Query execution divides its work into small units. A "work unit" might consist of examining a single index key, fetching a single document from the collection, applying a projection to a single document, or doing a piece of internal bookkeeping. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: explain plan, index
- [passage] For example, consider a query for `"item": "saccharomyces cerevisiae"` and `"stock": 60`. If the collection contains 10000 documents matching `"item": "saccharomyces cerevisiae"` and only 100 of those documents match `"stock": 60`, the query examines 10000 keys. In the `IXSCAN` stage, the query filters those keys by the `stock` field and only returns 100 results to the next stage. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#index-prefixes · keywords: index, plan stage, "item": "saccharomyces cerevisiae", "stock": 60, IXSCAN, stock
- [passage] For example, with a granularity of `seconds`, MongoDB buckets documents within the same hour. If a bucket contains a document with a `metaField` value of `sensorA` and a `timeField` value of `2024-08-01T18:23:21Z`, an incoming document with a `metaField` of `sensorB` goes into a separate bucket regardless of time. An incoming document from `sensorA` goes into the same bucket only if its `timeField` is between `2024-08-01T18:00:00Z` and `2024-08-01T18:59:59Z`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md#how-bucketing-works · keywords: executionStats, seconds, metaField, sensorA, timeField, 2024-08-01T18:23:21Z

- [passage] | Field | Necessity | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | [field](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-field) | Required | The field to densify. The values of the specified `field` must either be all numeric values or all dates. Documents that do not contain the specified `field` continue through the pipeline unmodified. To specify a `<field>` in an embedded document or in an array, use [dot notation.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/document.md#std-label-document-dot-notation) For restrictions, see [`field` Restrictions.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-field-restrictions) | | [partitionByFields](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-partition-by-fields) | Optional | The set of fields to act as the compound key to group the documents. In the [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) stage, each group of documents is known as a *partition*. If you omit this field, [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) uses one partition for the entire collection. For an example, see [Densification with Partitions.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-examples-partitions) For restrictions, see [`partitionByFields` Restrictions.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-partition-by-fields-restrictions) | | [range](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-range) | Required | An object that specifies how the data is densified. | | [range.bounds](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-bounds) | Required | You can specify `range.bounds` as either: An array: `[ < lower bound >, < upper bound > ]`,; A string: either `"full"` or `"partition"`. If `bounds` is an array: [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) adds documents spanning the range of values within the specified bounds.; The data type for the bounds must correspond to the data type in the [field](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-field) being densified.; For behavior details, see [`range.bounds` Behavior.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-bounds-behavior) If `bounds` is `"full"`: [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) adds documents spanning the full range of values of the `field` being densified. If `bounds` is `"partition"`: [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) adds documents to each partition, similar to if you had run a `full` range densification on each partition individually. | | [range.step](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-step) | Required | The amount to increment the [field](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-field) value in each document. [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) creates a new document for each `step` between the existing documents. If [range.unit](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-unit) is specified, `step` must be an integer. Otherwise, `step` can be any numeric value. | | [range.unit](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-unit) | Required if [field](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-field) is a date. | The unit to apply to the [step](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-step) field when incrementing date values in [field.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-field) You can specify one of the following values for `unit` as a string: `millisecond`; `second`; `minute`; `hour`; `day`; `week`; `month`; `quarter`; `year` For an example, see [Densify Time Series Data.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#std-label-densify-examples-time-series) | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#syntax · keywords: index bounds, field, <field>, $densify, partitionByFields, range.bounds
- [passage] In prior versions, [`$densify`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-densify) treats bounds with an equal lower and upper bound as a closed interval and generates a document with the bound value as a field value if the collection does not already contain a document with the bound value. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/densify.md#range-bounds-behavior · keywords: index bounds, $densify

## How it works

- [statement] The Atlas docs' worked example: a log line with planSummary COLLSCAN, keysExamined 0, docsExamined 10000, nreturned 4 gives a ratio of 2500. Atlas names a missing index or an index that only partially supports the query as the typical cause, and recommends Performance Advisor, Query Shape Reports and Query Targeting metrics for follow-up. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting/ · keywords: database profiler, executionStats, index, index effectiveness, plan stage, query shape
- [passage] The time reported by `explain.executionStats.executionTimeMillis` is not necessarily representative of actual query time. During steady state operations (when the query plan is cached), or when using [`cursor.hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) with `cursor.explain()`, MongoDB bypasses the plan selection process, resulting in a faster actual time, leading to a lower `explain.executionStats.executionTimeMillis` value. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, hint, query planner, explain.executionStats.executionTimeMillis, cursor.hint() · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] | Counter | Description | | --- | --- | | `collscan``clusteredCollscan` | Collection scans, counted separately based on whether the scan uses the [clustered index.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections.md#std-label-clustered-collections) | | `coveredIxscan` | Index scans that don't fetch documents. | | `ixscanFetch` | Index scans that fetch documents. | | `countScan` | Scans that count index keys without returning documents. | | `distinctScan``distinctScanFetch` | Scans that skip duplicate index keys, counted separately based on whether the scan fetches documents. | | `geoNear2d``geoNear2dSphere` | Geospatial proximity searches, counted separately based on whether the query uses a [2d](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2d.md#std-label-2d-index) or [2dsphere](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2dsphere.md#std-label-2dsphere-index) index. | | `textMatch` | Text searches that use a [text index.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text.md#std-label-index-type-text) | | `otherAccessPath` | Winning plans that don't use a collection scan, an index scan, a count scan, a distinct scan, or a geospatial access path. A plan that only performs a text search increments both `textMatch` and `otherAccessPath`. | | `btreeIxscan``wildcardIxscan``sparseIxscan``uniqueIxscan``hashedIxscan``multikeyIxscan` | Index scans, counted separately by index property. A single index scan can increment multiple of these counters. | | `boundsFullScan``boundsPoint``boundsBoundedRange``boundsMinKeyToValue``boundsValueToMaxKey``boundsMixture` | Index scans, counted separately by the index bounds that the scan uses. MongoDB increments `boundsMixture` when the scan uses more than one type of bound. | | `boundsUnionedSmall``boundsUnionedLarge` | Index scans where a field has multiple bounds, counted separately by the number of bounds. `boundsUnionedSmall` counts fields with 2 to 50 bounds, and `boundsUnionedLarge` counts fields with 51 or more bounds. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md#access-path-counters · keywords: database profiler, index, index bounds, plan stage, query planner, collscan
- [fact] When totalKeysExamined is far lower than totalDocsExamined, the docs say to inspect each stage in executionStats.executionStages and compare keysExamined with docsExamined per stage to find which stage failed to use the index. A totalKeysExamined of 0 with large totalDocsExamined indicates a pure collection scan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/explain-slow-queries/ · keywords: database profiler, executionStats, explain plan, index, Explain Plan Interpretation
- [fact] keysExamined counts both in-bounds and out-of-bounds keys. When index bounds have several key ranges, the scan examines out-of-bounds keys to skip from one range to the next, so keysExamined can exceed the matching key count without the index being bad. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, index, index bounds, Explain Plan Interpretation
- [passage] As with any hash function, two different plan cache query shapes may result in the same hash value. However, the occurrence of hash collisions between different plan cache query shapes is unlikely. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler/ · keywords: plan cache, query shape, explain plan · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] Because the query shapes are the same, the explain output has the same queryShapeHash for each of the examples, and the same planCacheShapeHash for each. For example: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: explain plan, plan cache, query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md
- [passage] Because the query shape is different from the shape in the previous section, the explain output has a different queryShapeHash from the previous example, and a different planCacheShapeHash. For example: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: explain plan, plan cache, query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md
- [passage] Float that represents the estimated number of index keys that the query planner predicts the plan to process. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: explain plan, index, query planner · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [fact] A cached plan is replanned when its re-run trial does more than internalQueryCacheEvictionRatio (reported default 10) times the work of the original trial. In SBE, SERVER-85238 uses this ratio as a multiplier on the winner's totalKeysExamined + totalDocsExamined as the replanning read budget. The default of 10 comes only from a third-party slide deck, not official docs. — https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/query-planner-88498371/88498371 · keywords: executionStats, plan cache, slot-based execution engine, Query Planning and Plan Cache
- [passage] When you create an index, you can give the index a custom name. Giving your index a name helps distinguish different indexes on your collection. For example, you can more easily identify the indexes used by a query in the query plan's [explain results](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-explain-results) if your indexes have distinct names. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/create-index/specify-index-name.md · keywords: explain plan, index, query planner
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 8.3, multi-planning with a CBR backup is the default plan selection mechanism for eligible queries. For a short trial period, the multi-planner attempts to find a plan capable of returning a result set within this short timeframe. If the attempt is unsuccessful, MongoDB applies a set of rules to determine whether the multi-planner should continue or if CBR should evaluate each node in the plan to determine the optimal plan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#queryplanner · keywords: explain plan, query planner · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/current/core/query-plans/
- [passage] When you sort based on an array field that is indexed with a multikey index, the query plan includes an in-memory sort stage unless both of the following are true: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/ · keywords: index, plan stage, query planner · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes/
- [passage] `notablescan` does not allow unbounded queries that use a clustered index because the queries require a full collection scan. For more information, see [Collection Scans.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-explain-output-collection-scan) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: database profiler, explain plan, index, notablescan
- [passage] - [`executionStats.totalKeysExamined`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.executionStats.totalKeysExamined) displays `3809` to indicate that MongoDB scanned 3,809 index entries. The number of keys examined match the number of documents returned, meaning that the [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) only had to examine index keys to return the results. The [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) did not have to scan all of the documents, and only the 3,809 matching documents had to be pulled into memory. This results in a very efficient query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, index, executionStats.totalKeysExamined, 3809, mongod · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan/
- [passage] When the slot-based query execution engine is used for [`$group`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/group.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-group), the [explain results](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-explain-results) include `queryPlanner.winningPlan.queryPlan.stage: "GROUP"`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-optimization.md#group-optimization · keywords: explain plan, query planner, $group, queryPlanner.winningPlan.queryPlan.stage: "GROUP"

- [passage] - `heuristics`: Uses a set of rules to determine selectivity. - [passage] - If the `$facet` stage comes later in the pipeline and earlier stages have used indexes, `$facet` will not trigger a `COLLSCAN` during execution. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/facet.md#index-use · keywords: database profiler, index, plan stage, $facet, COLLSCAN
- [passage] For example, [`$match`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/match.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-match) or [`$sort`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sort.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-sort) stages that come before a `$facet` stage can make use of indexes and the `$facet` will not trigger a `COLLSCAN`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/facet.md#index-use · keywords: database profiler, index, plan stage, $match, $sort, $facet
- [passage] With Queryable Encryption, MongoDB tracks the occurrences of each field/value pair in an encrypted collection using an internal counter. The [contention factor](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-contention-factor) partitions this counter, similar to an array. This minimizes issues with incrementing the counter when using `insert`, `update`, or `findAndModify` to add or modify an encrypted field with the same field/value pair in close succession. `contention = 0` creates an array with one element at index 0. `contention = 4` creates an array with 5 elements at indexes 0-4. MongoDB increments a random array element during insert. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/encrypt-and-query.md#advanced-query-parameters · keywords: executionStats, index, insert, update, findAndModify, contention = 0
- [passage] Last point queries are most performant when they use the [DISTINCT\_SCAN optimization](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-explain-results). This optimization is only available when an index on `timeField` is descending. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-secondary-index.md#last-point-queries-on-time-series-collections · keywords: explain plan, index, timeField
- [passage] Bounds intersection refers to the point where multiple bounds overlap. For example, given the bounds `[ [ 3, Infinity ] ]` and `[ [ -Infinity, 6 ] ]`, the intersection of the bounds results in `[ [ 3, 6 ] ]`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#bounds-intersection-for-a-multikey-index · keywords: index, index bounds, [ [ 3, Infinity ] ], [ [ -Infinity, 6 ] ], [ [ 3, 6 ] ]
- [passage] Because the query uses `$elemMatch` to join these predicates, MongoDB intersects the bounds to: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#example-bounds-intersection · keywords: index, index bounds, $elemMatch
- [passage] Because the preceding query does not use `$elemMatch`, MongoDB does not intersect the bounds. Instead, MongoDB uses either of the following bounds: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#query-without-elemmatch · keywords: index, index bounds, $elemMatch
- [passage] When an index covers a query, the explain result has an `IXSCAN` stage that is **not** a descendant of a `FETCH` stage. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#covered-queries · keywords: index, plan stage, IXSCAN, FETCH · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] Limits how many digits after the decimal point are taken into account when querying a `double` or `decimal` field. Additional digits are dropped, not rounded. For example, a `precision` of 1 treats `10.18` as `10.1` for queries. The encrypted value is still stored as `10.18`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/encrypt-and-query.md#advanced-query-parameters · keywords: executionStats, double, decimal, precision, 10.18, 10.1
- [passage] When unset, `contention` defaults to `8`, which provides high performance for most workloads. Higher contention improves the performance of insert and update operations on low cardinality fields, but decreases find performance. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/encrypt-and-query.md#advanced-query-parameters · keywords: executionStats, contention
- [passage] Because `metaField` values must match exactly to group documents, the number of buckets in a time series collection depends on the number of unique `metaField` values. Collections with fine-grained or changing `metaField` values generate many sparsely packed, short-lived buckets. This leads to decreased storage and query efficiency. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md#how-the-metafield-affects-bucketing · keywords: executionStats, metaField
- [passage] 4. Queryable Encryption implements a fast, searchable scheme that allows the server to process queries on fully encrypted data, without knowing anything about the data. The data and the query itself remain encrypted at all times on the server. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/features.md#how-queryable-encryption-works · keywords: executionStats
- [passage] Setting [`cursorTimeoutMillis`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.cursorTimeoutMillis) to less than or equal to `0` results in all cursors being immediately eligible for timeout. Generally, the timeout value should be greater than the average amount of time for a query to return results. Use tools like the [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) cursor modifier to analyze the average query time and select an appropriate timeout period. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: explain plan, cursorTimeoutMillis, cursor.explain()
- [passage] **Index bounds** define the range of index values that MongoDB searches when using an index to fulfill a query. When you specify multiple query predicates on an indexed field, MongoDB attempts to combine the bounds for those predicates to produce an index scan with smaller bounds. Smaller index bounds result in faster queries and reduced resource use. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md · keywords: index, index bounds
- [passage] Compound bounds combine bounds for multiple keys of a [compound index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#std-label-index-type-compound). Using bounds from multiple keys reduces the time it takes to process a query because MongoDB does not need to compute results for each bound individually. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#compound-bounds-for-a-multikey-index · keywords: index, index bounds
- [passage] The following example shows how MongoDB uses compound bounds when an index includes a non-array field and multiple array fields. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#example-compound-bounds-of-non-array-field-and-multiple-array-fields · keywords: index, index bounds
- [passage] The fields `"ratings.scores.q1"` and `"ratings.scores.q2"` share the field path `"ratings.scores"`. In order to compound index bounds, a query must use `$elemMatch` on the common field path. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#example-elemmatch-on-diverging-field-paths · keywords: index, index bounds, "ratings.scores.q1", "ratings.scores.q2", "ratings.scores", $elemMatch
- [passage] Specifies the *inclusive* lower bound for a specific index in order to constrain the results of [`find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find). [`min()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.min.md#mongodb-method-cursor.min) provides a way to specify lower bounds on compound key indexes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.min.md#definition · keywords: index, index bounds, find(), min()
- [passage] The Explain Plan doesn't show aggregation pipeline stages such as [`$merge`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-merge) and [`$out`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/out.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-out) because Atlas ignores all out stages from the aggregation before running the explain plan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/query-plan.md#about-this-task · keywords: explain plan, $merge, $out
- [passage] Index scans, counted separately by the index bounds that the scan uses. MongoDB increments boundsMixture when the scan uses more than one type of bound. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: index, index bounds
- [passage] `$in` compares each parameter to each document in the collection, which can cause performance issues. To improve performance, create an index on the `field` you want to query. An index allows MongoDB to create bounds for each `$in` element and search more efficiently. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/in.md#syntax · keywords: index, index bounds, $in, field
- [passage] For example, `$group` operations of the following form can result in a `DISTINCT_SCAN`: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/group.md#retrieve-distinct-values · keywords: plan stage, $group, DISTINCT_SCAN
- [passage] Number of post-recovery waits that completed when the cluster's config time advanced since the server started. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#shard · keywords: executionStats
- [passage] usedDisk is true when the query writes data to temporary files due to memory restrictions. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: executionStats
- [passage] MongoDB follows prevaling database usage and works with time in UTC. The `dateSubtract` expression always takes a `startDate` in UTC and returns a result in UTC. If the `timezone` is specified, the calculation will be done using the specified `timezone`. The timezone is especially important when a calculation involves Daylight Savings Time (DST). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/dateSubtract.md#time-measurement · keywords: executionStats, dateSubtract, startDate, timezone · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/dateAdd.md
- [passage] - When you specify Polygon `coordinates`, the first and last coordinates in the array must be the same. - [passage] The sort direction is descending because the `sortBy` value is "-1". — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sortArray.md#sort-on-a-subfield · keywords: index bounds, sortBy

## How-to and procedures

- [passage] To see whether MongoDB will apply an index filter for a plan cache query shape, check the [`indexFilterSet`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.queryPlanner.indexFilterSet) field of either the [`db.collection.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.explain) or the [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) method. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheSetFilter.md#set-filter-on-plan-cache-query-shape-consisting-of-predicate-only · keywords: explain plan, index, plan cache, query settings, query shape, indexFilterSet
- [passage] Use the [`db.collection.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.explain) or the [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) method in [executionStats](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#std-label-explain-method-executionStats) mode to return statistics about the query process, including the index used, the number of documents scanned, and the time the query takes to process in milliseconds. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/measure-index-use.md#return-query-plan-with-explain · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, index, query planner, db.collection.explain(), cursor.explain() · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md
- [passage] Run [`db.collection.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.explain) or the [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) method in [allPlansExecution](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#std-label-explain-method-allPlansExecution) mode to view partial execution statistics collected during plan selection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/measure-index-use.md#return-query-plan-with-explain · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, query planner, db.collection.explain(), cursor.explain()
- [fact] To compare candidate indexes, run the same query with hint() and explain('executionStats') and compare totalKeysExamined. In the MongoDB docs example, {year:1, rated:1} scanned 246 keys for 235 results while {rated:1, year:1} scanned 235, so the second is more efficient (equality field before range field). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan/ · keywords: executionStats, hint, index, index effectiveness, Index Effectiveness Measurement
- [passage] To view the query plan selected, chain the [`cursor.explain("executionStats")`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) cursor method to the end of the **find** command: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, query planner, cursor.explain("executionStats") · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan/
- [passage] To view the MongoDB 8.0 queryShapeHash and planCacheShapeHash hexadecimal strings, you can use the explain command. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: explain plan, plan cache, query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md
- [passage] To hide a text index, you must specify the index by `name` and not by `keyPattern`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/collMod.md#hide-an-index-from-the-query-planner · keywords: index, index bounds, query planner, name, keyPattern
- [passage] To view the execution statistics for a specific index, append to the [`db.collection.find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find) the [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) method followed by [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain), e.g.: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/measure-index-use.md#control-index-use-with-hint · keywords: explain plan, hint, index, db.collection.find(), hint(), cursor.explain()
- [passage] To manually compare the performance of a query using more than one index, you can use the [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) method in conjunction with the [`explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) method. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: explain plan, hint, index, hint(), explain()
- [passage] To manually compare the performance of a query using more than one index, you can use the hint() method in conjunction with the explain() method. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan/ · keywords: explain plan, hint, index

However, `kyber` is only available on linux kernels starting in version 4.12. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/production-checklist-operations.md#linux · keywords: executionStats, kyber

## Measurements and reference values

- [passage] nreturned:4 protocol:op_query 358ms — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting/ · keywords: executionStats
- [passage] For example, on a system with a total of 4GB of RAM the WiredTiger cache uses 1.5GB of RAM (`0.5 * (4GB - 1GB) = 1.5 GB`). When providing a specific cache size ensure the RAM does not exceed the bounds of 0.256GB to 10000GB. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/production-notes.md#cache-configuration-settings · keywords: index bounds, 0.5 * (4GB - 1GB) = 1.5 GB

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [passage] | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | `version` | A number that indicates the query engine used to complete the query. `1` indicates that the classic engine was used.; `2` indicates that the [slot-based query execution engine](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/sbe.md#std-label-sbe-landing) was used. | | `createdFromQuery` | A document that contains the specific query that resulted in this cache entry. For example: `{ "query" : <document>, "sort" : <document>, "projection" : <document> }` | | `isActive` | A boolean that indicates whether the entry is active or inactive. If active, the query planner is currently using the entry to generate query plans.; If inactive, the query planner is not currently using the entry to generate query plans. See [Plan Cache Entry State.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-state) | | `planCacheShapeHash` | A hexadecimal string that represents the hash of the [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-query-shape). See [`explain.queryPlanner.planCacheShapeHash`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.queryPlanner.planCacheShapeHash) Starting in MongoDB 8.0, the existing `queryHash` field is duplicated in a new field named `planCacheShapeHash`. If you're using an earlier MongoDB version, you'll only see the `queryHash` field. Future MongoDB versions will remove the deprecated `queryHash` field, and you'll need to use the `planCacheShapeHash` field instead. | | `planCacheKey` | A hexadecimal string that represents the hash of the key used to find the plan cache entry associated with this query. The plan cache key is a function of both the [plan cache query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-plan-cache-query-shape) and the currently available indexes for that shape. See [`explain.queryPlanner.planCacheKey`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.queryPlanner.planCacheKey) | | `cachedPlan` | The details of the cached plan. The fields included in the `cachedPlan` vary based on whether the query was completed using the classic engine or the slot-based query execution engine. For more information on query plans, see [`explain.queryPlanner`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.queryPlanner) | | `works` | The number of "work units" performed by the query execution plan during the trial period when the query planner evaluates candidate plans. For more information, see [`explain.executionStats.executionStages.works`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.executionStats.executionStages.works) | | `timeOfCreation` | Time of creation for the entry. | | `creationExecStats` | An array of execution stats documents. The array contains a document for each candidate plan. For details on the execution stats, see [`explain.executionStats`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.executionStats) | | `candidatePlanScores` | An array of scores for the candidate plans listed in the `creationExecStats` array. | | `indexFilterSet` | A boolean that indicates whether an [index filter](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-index-filters) exists for the [plan cache query shape.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-plan-cache-query-shape) | | `estimatedSizeBytes` | The estimated size in bytes of a plan cache entry. | | `querySettings` | **New in version 8.0** A document that contains query settings previously set using [`setQuerySettings`:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) `querySettings: { indexHints: [ { ns: { db: <string>, coll: <string> }, allowedIndexes: <array> }, ... ], queryFramework: <string> }` `querySettings` fields: `indexHints.ns` (document): Namespace for index hints.`db` (string): Name of the database for index hints.; `coll` (string): Name of the collection for index hints.; `indexHints.allowedIndexes` (array): Array of indexes for index hints. For more details, see [Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes.md#std-label-indexes) and [`hint()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint); `queryFramework` (string): [Query framework](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-query-framework) string can be:`classic` for the classic engine.; `sbe` for slot-based query execution engine. For details, see [Slot-Based Query Execution Engine.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/sbe.md#std-label-sbe-landing) | | `host` | The hostname and port of the [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) instance from which the plan cache information was returned. When run on a sharded cluster, the operation returns plan cache entry information from a single member in each shard replica set. This member is identified with the [shard](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/plancachestats.md#std-label-plancachestats-shard) and [host](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/plancachestats.md#std-label-plancachestats-host) fields. See also [Redaction.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/plancachestats.md#std-label-plancachestats-read-pref) | | `shard` | The name of the shard from which [`$planCacheStats`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/plancachestats.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-planCacheStats) retrieved the cache entry. Only available if run on a sharded cluster. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/planCacheStats.md#classic-execution-engine · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, hint, index, plan cache, query planner

- [passage] | **MongoDB Version** | **Changes** | | --- | --- | | 6.1 | Slow operation log messages include [cache refresh time fields.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-messages-cache-refresh-times) | | 6.2 | Slow operation log messages include a `queryFramework` field that indicates which query engine executed the query: `queryFramework: "classic"` indicates that the classic engine executed the query.; `queryFramework: "sbe"` indicates that the slot-based query execution engine executed the query. | | 6.3 | Slow operation log messages and [database profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) entries include a `cpuNanos` field that specifies the total CPU time spent by a query operation in nanoseconds. The `cpuNanos` field is only available on Linux systems. | | 7.0 (and 6.0.13, 5.0.24) | The `totalOplogSlotDurationMicros` in the slow query log message shows the time between a write operation getting a commit timestamp to commit the storage engine writes and actually committing. `mongod` supports parallel writes. However, it commits write operations with commit timestamps in any order. For example, consider the following writes with commit timestamps: writeA with Timestamp1; writeB with Timestamp2; writeC with Timestamp3 Suppose writeB commits first at Timestamp2. Replication is paused until writeA commits because writeA's oplog entry with Timestamp1 is required for replication to copy the oplog to secondary replica set members. | | 8.0 | The slow query output includes a `queues` document that contains information about the operation's [queues](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverstatus.md#std-label-server-status-queues). Each queue in the `queues` field contains a `totalTimeQueuedMicros` field that contains the total cumulative time in microseconds that the operation spent in the corresponding queue. The `queryShapeHash` field for a [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes) is also included in the slow query log when available. If a command with a specific query shape is [rejected](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/operation-rejection-filters.md#std-label-operation-rejection-filters), MongoDB logs a message that states the query command was rejected. The message contains the query namespace, `queryShapeHash`, and the command with the rejected query. MongoDB only logs the message if the log verbosity level is set to at least `2`. | | 8.1 | Slow query log messages contain new metrics if the query execution writes temporary files to disk. These metrics are prefixed by the query execution stage that caused the query to exceed the memory limit. For example, `sortSpills` indicates the number of times that the sort stage of query execution wrote temporary files to disk. `<executionPart>Spills` indicates the number of times the corresponding query execution stage wrote temporary files to disk.; `<executionPart>SpilledBytes` indicates the size, in bytes, of the memory released by writing temporary files to disk.; `<executionPart>SpilledDataStorageSize` indicates the size, in bytes, of disk space used for temporary files.; `<executionPart>SpilledRecords` indicates the number of records written to temporary files on disk. For more information on writing temporary files to disk, see [`allowDiskUse()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowdiskuse.md#mongodb-method-cursor.allowDiskUse) | | 8.3 | Slow query log entries have an optional `originalQueryShapeHash` field that contains that query shape of the following operations that originate on the [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#std-program-mongos) : [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find); [`aggregate`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/aggregate.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.aggregate); [`count`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/count.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.count); [`distinct`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/distinct.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.distinct) The original query shape of the `mongos` operation may differ after the `mongos` sends the operation to the [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#std-program-mongod) . MongoDB 8.3 also introduces slow in-progress query log entries. Queries trigger a slow-in progress log during execution. These logs contain less information than standard slow query logs. MongoDB logs queries at most once if the query's duration surpasses the [`operationProfiling.slowOpInProgressThresholdMs`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-operationProfiling.slowOpInProgressThresholdMs) When an operation specifies a [time limit for a query](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-documents/specify-query-timeout.md#std-label-manual-query-timeout), slow query logs contain a `deadline` field. `deadline` indicates the time the operation must complete by, which is equal to the time at the start of the operation plus the value of the query timeout. | | 9.0 | When a query shape has query knobs set through [`setQuerySettings`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) or [`setParameter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setparameter.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setParameter), slow query log entries include a `queryKnobs` document. The document shows the effective value of each knob and where the value comes from, with the same shape as the [explain output](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-explain-output-query-knobs). For details, see [Query Knobs.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#std-label-setQuerySettings-query-knobs) | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#version-specific-changes · keywords: database profiler, executionStats, explain plan, plan stage, query settings, query shape
- [statement] Before dropping, check prefix redundancy (a compound index { a:1, b:1 } serves queries on { a:1 }), and after dropping watch the slow-query log for COLLSCAN and verify critical query shapes with explain('executionStats'), since the planner may switch to a different existing index. — https://www.netdata.cloud/guides/mongodb/mongodb-unused-indexes/ · keywords: $indexStats, database profiler, executionStats, index, plan stage, query planner
- [fact] planSummary is a string in both system.profile documents and slow-query log entries that summarises the winning plan (e.g. 'COLLSCAN' or 'IXSCAN { a: 1, _id: -1 }'). A COLLSCAN with keysExamined 0 and docsExamined far above nreturned signals a missing index; the docsExamined:docsReturned ratio near 1:1 is ideal. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler/ · keywords: database profiler, executionStats, index, plan stage, query planner, query shape
- [passage] | Method | Availability | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | Use the Atlas Query Profiler | M10+ Atlas clusters | The Atlas Query Profiler shows long-running operations and performance statistics. For more information, see [Monitor Query Performance with the Query Profiler.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#std-label-profile-database) | | Enable the Database Profiler | Atlas clusters and self-hosted deployments | When enabled, the database profiler stores information about slow queries in the [`system.profile`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/system-collections.md#mongodb-data--database-.system.profile) collection. - [passage] When a query shape has query knobs set through setQuerySettings or setParameter, slow query log entries include a queryKnobs document. The document shows the effective value of each knob and where the value comes from, with the same shape as the explain output. - [fact] A SORT stage means an in-memory sort. In stages that can spill, usedDisk true (added in 5.3) shows the sort went to disk, which is slow; the usual fix is a compound index whose order supports the sort so the SORT stage disappears. — https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-read-executionstats-output-explain/view · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, index, plan stage, Explain Plan Interpretation
- [fact] From 8.0 the explain output carries planCacheShapeHash (a copy of queryHash, which is deprecated and slated for removal) and planCacheKey. planCacheKey depends on both the plan cache query shape and the available indexes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: explain plan, index, plan cache, query shape, Explain Plan Interpretation
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 8.0, the existing `queryHash` field is duplicated in a new field named `planCacheShapeHash`. If you're using an earlier MongoDB version, you'll only see the `queryHash` field. Future MongoDB versions will remove the deprecated `queryHash` field, and you'll need to use the `planCacheShapeHash` field instead. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#plancacheshapehash · keywords: plan cache, query shape, explain plan, queryHash, planCacheShapeHash · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getMore.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/planCacheStats.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheClear.md
- [passage] A hexadecimal string that represents the hash of the [plan cache query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-plan-cache-query-shape) and is dependent only on the plan cache query shapes. `planCacheShapeHash` can help identify slow queries (including the query filter of write operations) with the same plan cache query shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: explain plan, plan cache, query shape, planCacheShapeHash · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] - If `false` or `0`, the stage may still have results to return. For example, consider a query with a limit whose execution stages consists of a `LIMIT` stage with an input stage of `IXSCAN` for the query. If the query returns more than the specified limit, the `LIMIT` stage will report `isEOF: 1`, but its underlying `IXSCAN` stage will report `isEOF: 0`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: executionStats, explain plan, plan stage, false, LIMIT, IXSCAN · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] To check if MongoDB must perform an in-memory sort, append cursor.explain() to the query and check the explain results. If the query plan contains a SORT stage, then MongoDB must perform an in-memory sort operation subject to the 100 megabyte memory limit. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowDiskUse/ · keywords: explain plan, plan stage, query planner · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowDiskUse.md
- [passage] | Index Property | Description | | --- | --- | | `expireAfterSeconds` | The number of seconds that determines the expiration threshold of a [TTL Collection.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/expire-data.md#std-label-ttl-collections) If successful, the command returns a document that contains: `expireAfterSeconds_new`, the new value for `expireAfterSeconds`; `expireAfterSeconds_old`, the old value for `expireAfterSeconds`, if the index had a value for `expireAfterSeconds` before. Modifying the index option `expireAfterSeconds` resets the [`$indexStats`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/indexstats.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-indexStats) for the index. If you use TTL indexes created before MongoDB 5.0, or if you want to sync data created in MongDB 5.0 with a pre-5.0 installation, see [Indexes Configured Using NaN](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/expire-data.md#std-label-expireData-warning) to avoid misconfiguration issues. The TTL index `expireAfterSeconds` value must be within `0` and `2147483647` inclusive. | | `hidden` | A boolean that determines whether the index is [hidden](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden.md#std-label-index-type-hidden) or not from the query planner. If the `hidden` value changes, the command returns a document that contains both the old and new values for the changed property: `hidden_old` and `hidden_new`. However, if the `hidden` value has not changed (i.e. hiding an already hidden index or unhiding an already unhidden index), the command omits the `hidden_old` and `hidden_new` fields from the output. To hide an index, you must have [featureCompatibilityVersion](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setfeaturecompatibilityversion.md#std-label-view-fcv) set to `4.4` or greater. Modifying the index option `hidden` resets the [`$indexStats`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/indexstats.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-indexStats) for the index if the value changes. | | `prepareUnique` | A boolean that determines whether the index will accept new duplicate entries. New duplicate entries fail with DuplicateKey errors when `prepareUnique` is `true`. The resulting index can be converted to a unique index. To convert the index, use `collMod` with the `unique` option. If an existing index is updated so that `prepareUnique` is `true`, the index is not checked for pre-existing, duplicate index entries. **New in version 6.0** | | `unique` | A boolean that determines whether the index is unique. A value of `false` is not supported. When `unique` is `true`, `collMod` scans the `keyPattern` index for duplicates and then converts it to a unique index if there are no duplicate index entries. If duplicates are detected during the initial scan, `collMod` returns `CannotConvertIndexToUnique` and a list of conflicting documents. To convert an index with duplicate entries to a unique index, correct any reported conflicts and rerun `collMod`. To end a conversion, set `prepareUnique` to `false`. To see an example of how to convert a non-unique index to a unique index, see [Convert an Existing Index to a Unique Index.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique/convert-to-unique.md#std-label-index-convert-to-unique) **New in version 6.0** | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/collMod.md#change-index-properties · keywords: $indexStats, index, index bounds, query planner, expireAfterSeconds, expireAfterSeconds_new
- [passage] If MongoDB cannot use an index or indexes to obtain the sort order, the results include a `SORT` stage indicating an in-memory sort operation. If the explain plan does not contain an explicit `SORT` stage, then MongoDB used an index to obtain the sort order. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#sort-stage · keywords: explain plan, index, plan stage, SORT · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | [setIndexCommitQuorum](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum.md#std-label-setIndexCommitQuorum-cmd-coll) | `string` | The name of the collection for which the indexes are being built. | | [indexNames](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum.md#std-label-setIndexCommitQuorum-cmd-indexNames) | `array` | An array of in-progress index builds to modify. Each element of the array must be the *name* of the index. The indexes specified to `indexNames` must be the entire set of in-progress builds associated to a given index builder, i.e. the indexes built by a single [`createIndexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createindexes.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.createIndexes) or [`db.collection.createIndexes()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindexes.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.createIndexes) operation. | | [commitQuorum](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum.md#std-label-setIndexCommitQuorum-cmd-commitQuorum) | `int` or `string` | The minimum number of data-bearing replica set members (i.e. commit quorum), including the primary, that must report a successful [index build](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-operations-replicated-build) before the primary marks the `indexes` as ready. You can resume some [interrupted index builds](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-operations-build-failure) when the commit quorum is set to the default `"votingMembers"`. To update the commitQuorum, member replica set nodes must have [`members[n].buildIndexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/replica-configuration.md#mongodb-rsconf-rsconf.members-n-.buildIndexes) set to `true`. If any voting nodes have `members[n].buildIndexes` set to `false`, you can't use the default `"votingMembers"` commit quorum. Either configure all nodes with `members[n].buildIndexes` set to `true`, or select a different commit quorum. Supports the following values: `"votingMembers"` - all data-bearing voting replica set members (*Default*). A "voting" member is any replica set member where [`members[n].votes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/replica-configuration.md#mongodb-rsconf-rsconf.members-n-.votes) is greater than `0`.; `"majority"` - a simple majority of data-bearing replica set members.; `<int>` - a specific number of data-bearing replica set members. Specify an integer greater than `0`.; A replica set [tag name.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/configure-replica-set-tag-sets.md) | | `comment` | any | Optional. A comment can be any valid [BSON type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bson-types.md#std-label-bson-types) (string, integer, object, array, etc). | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setIndexCommitQuorum.md#command-fields · keywords: $currentOp, database profiler, index, index bounds, string, array
- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `key` | document | Specifies the index's fields. For each field, specify a key-value pair in which the key is the name of the field to index and the value is either the index direction or [index type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types.md#std-label-index-types). [Collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) allows users to specify language-specific rules for string comparison, such as rules for lettercase and accent marks. If you have specified a collation at the collection level, then: If you do not specify a collation when creating the index, MongoDB creates the index with the collection's default collation.; If you do specify a collation when creating the index, MongoDB creates the index with the specified collation. The collation option has the following syntax: `collation: { locale: <string>, caseLevel: <boolean>, caseFirst: <string>, strength: <int>, numericOrdering: <boolean>, alternate: <string>, maxVariable: <string>, backwards: <boolean> }` When specifying collation, the `locale` field is mandatory; all other collation fields are optional. For descriptions of the fields, see [Collation Document.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation-document-fields) | | `wildcardProjection` | document | Optional. Allows users to include or exclude specific field paths from a [wildcard index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard.md#std-label-wildcard-index-core) using the `{ "$**" : 1}` key pattern. This option is only valid if creating a [wildcard index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard.md#std-label-wildcard-index-core) on all document fields. You cannot specify this option if creating a wildcard index on a specific field path and its subfields, e.g. `{ "path.to.field.$**" : 1 }` The `wildcardProjection` option takes the following form: `wildcardProjection: { "path.to.field.a" : <value>, "path.to.field.b" : <value> }` The `<value>` can be either of the following: `1` or `true` to include the field in the wildcard index.; `0` or `false` to exclude the field from the wildcard index. Wildcard indexes omit the `_id` field by default. To include the `_id` field in the wildcard index, you must explicitly include it in the `wildcardProjection` document: `{ "wildcardProjection": { "_id": 1, "<field>": 0|1 } }` All of the statements in the `wildcardProjection` document must be either inclusion or exclusion statements. You can also include the `_id` field with exclusion statements. This is the only exception to the rule. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md#command-fields · keywords: index, index bounds, query planner, key,  for ascending or , name

Supports the following values: `"votingMembers"` - all data-bearing voting replica set members (*Default*).; `"majority"` - a simple majority of data-bearing voting replica set members.; `<int>` - a specific number of data-bearing voting replica set members.; `0` - Disables quorum-voting behavior.
